newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria president will not seek Socialist govt.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria president will not seek Socialist govt.

text.p: Bulgarian President Zhelyu Zhelev, who was due to ask the Socialists to form a new government on Saturday, said he would no longer do so after an unprecedented day-long siege of parliament by the opposition.

"Under these conditions, tomorrow I will not give a mandate for formation of a new government. I am convening the National Security Council," Zhelev said on national television. The council advises the president on internal and external security matters.
"I back the protests of the people who have been driven to this humiliating state. In this way they are demonstrating their dignity," said Zhelev, in a reference to the country's economic crisis.
"I do not approve of violence and appeal for order."
Opposition deputies earlier walked out of parliament after failing to reach agreement with the ex-communist ruling Socialists on a declaration calling for early elections.
The Socialists had been expected to form a new government after the resignation of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov on December 21.
